alignment.method: Least-squares Kabsch rigid-body alignment, without reflection, onto deposited 7W38.
alignment.selection: Identity-verified C-alpha positions common to all six structures and 7W38 in all 28 20S core chains G–T,g–t. Alpha-subunit residues 1–30 are excluded to avoid fitting moving N-terminal gates.
alignment.coordinateStatus: All exported frame coordinates are already aligned; do not apply the saved transform again.

correspondence.missingResidues: Full observedFrames preserve every positive-occupancy deposited C-alpha atom. Common frames contain only identity-verified residues present in all six states. Both representations split at sequence gaps or C-alpha distances greater than 5 angstrom. No missing positions are created.
correspondence.usp14Note: ED5 models USP14 residues 103–494; the other five states model residues 1–494. The common USP14 comparison contains 392 residues, and the additional 102 residues are shown only in observed endpoint frames.

metrics.selection: Only sequence-verified residues common to all six states, after alignment to 7W38. Unassigned substrate excluded. Displacements compare modeled C-alpha coordinates and do not measure speed, force, or per-residue physical trajectories.

limitations: Experimental structures are ensemble snapshots from separate cryo-EM classes, not frames of one tracked molecule.
Published state ordering is mechanistic inference. Playback intervals and optional interpolated coordinates have no experimental kinetic meaning.
Linear interpolation is a geometric illustration and can distort protein geometry; it is not molecular dynamics or an energy-minimized pathway.
Only C-alpha atoms are displayed. Full deposited atomic coordinates remain available in the source files.
The EMD-32273 density belongs to 7W38 and must not be shown as density evidence for these six conformations.

sources.orderBasis: Article section “Asymmetric ATP hydrolysis around ATPase ring”, Fig. 3c and Extended Data Fig. 7i,j; six-state segment ED4→ED5→ED0→ED1→ED2.0→ED2.1.
